Article Title: BJP’s Bengal poll spend alone tops Congress’ Rs 249 crore outlay across 5 states, finds ECI
Article Text:
Bengal BJP spending on polls

BJP’s Bengal spending outpaces Congress’ five-state total

Congress spent more than BJP in Kerala

NEW DELHI: The BJP spent Rs 286.99 crore on the West Bengal elections alone, more than the Rs 248.55 crore the Congress spent across five states and a Union territory that went to polls earlier this year, according to expenditure statements filed with the Election Commission.West Bengal accounted for more than half of the BJP’s total expenditure of Rs 529.38 crore across the five elections — in West Bengal, Assam, Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Puducherry.The BJP spent Rs 217.16 crore on general campaigning in Bengal and another Rs 69.83 crore on candidates and related expenses, news agency PTI reported.The party came to power in West Bengal for the first time, winning 207 of the 293 seats for which results were declared.The Congress, which contested 293 seats independently in Bengal despite having a limited presence in the state, won two seats. It reported spending Rs 42.08 crore in Bengal through its central headquarters and state unit.Of this, Rs 12.96 crore was spent on general campaigning, while Rs 29.12 crore went towards candidates and related expenses.The CPI(M), which ruled Bengal for decades before losing power in 2011, contested 197 seats and won one.Its state unit reported expenditure of Rs 8.23 crore, including spending on candidates.The expenditure statement of the Trinamool Congress, the BJP’s principal rival in Bengal, has not been made public yet.Kerala presented a different spending pattern. The Congress-led alliance displaced the CPI(M)-led Left Democratic Front, with the Congress winning 63 seats and the CPI(M) 26. The BJP won three seats.The Congress spent Rs 105.34 crore in Kerala through its headquarters and state unit, higher than the BJP’s Rs 82.67 crore.Of the Congress’ expenditure, Rs 71.30 crore went towards general campaigning and Rs 34.05 crore towards candidates and related expenses.The BJP reported spending Rs 54.93 crore on general campaigning in Kerala and Rs 27.74 crore on candidates.
Article Summary: BJP came to power in West Bengal for the first time, winning 207 of the 293 seats for which results were declared. Congress, which contested 293 seats independently in Bengal despite having a limited presence in the state, won two seats. BJP reported spending Rs 54.93 crore on general campaigning in Kerala and Rs 27.74 crore on candidates.

Article Title: 'If pardoned for one murder, I'd shoot Gyanesh': VIP chief targets CEC over SIR row
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: "If I were pardoned for one murder, the first person I would shoot is Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar!" former Bihar minister and Vikassheel Insaan Party (VIP) chief Mukesh Sahani said on Thursday amid the ongoing row over the functioning of the Election Commission Speaking to reporters, Sahani accused the Election Commission of acting at the BJP's behest and warned that those involved could face jail if the opposition came to power in 2029."The Election Commission has turned into an arm of the BJP. And I want to say to Gyanesh Kumar: times do not stay the same forever. Have some shame - you are playing with the nation's Constitution! If I were pardoned for one murder, the first person I would shoot is Gyanesh! But what can we do? We are law-abiding citizens who respect the Constitution," Sahani said."In the times ahead, they will not go scot-free. In 2029, a government will be formed in the country under the leadership of Rahul Gandhi ji, and Gyanesh Kumar will be the very first person sent to prison. Everyone who colluded with him will also go to jail; no one will be spared. If he passes away before that, that is another matter. But if they remain alive, they will be put behind bars - there are no ifs or buts about it. Nobody will be able to protect him, not even Modi ji.In fact, Modi ji might also end up in jail!" he claimed.Sahani's remarks come after an Indian Express report flagged differences within the poll panel over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. According to the report, Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi formally objected at least 14 times over 10 months to decisions and orders issued in connection with electoral-roll procedures.The Election Commission, meanwhile, said the reported queries and observations by its members were part of its normal internal functioning. The poll panel said written notes, technical suggestions and internal checks were standard practices aimed at ensuring legal compliance and safeguarding voter rights.The ECI also maintained that all its official decisions, including those concerning SIR, had full legal sanction and that the Commission's final decisions were unanimous.The report triggered sharp reactions from Opposition parties, with several leaders demanding greater scrutiny of the Election Commission's decision-making process and questioning Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's functioning.The BJP, meanwhile, defended the poll panel and said internal deliberations were part of democratic functioning.
Article Summary: Mukesh Sahani accuses the Election Commission of acting at the BJP's behest. Former Bihar minister warns those involved could face jail if the opposition comes to power in 2029. Indian Express report flagged differences within the poll panel over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

There are exhibitions that showcase products. There are conferences that bring people together for conversations. And then there are platforms that gradually become an ecosystem of their own.HOSPEX began as an idea at a difficult moment for healthcare, the COVID-19 pandemic. The journey of HOSPEX has been anything but straightforward and empowering. Behind the numbers and the growing exhibition floor is a team that has experienced the highs and lows of building an event from the ground up.There were moments of uncertainty, last-minute challenges and difficult decisions. There were also moments of pride, watching the exhibition come alive, seeing people connect for the first time, and witnessing an idea that started small, gradually becoming a larger healthcare community.The team has grown with the event. The pandemic had exposed both the strengths and vulnerabilities of healthcare systems. It demonstrated the importance of medical technology, diagnostics, digital health, medical devices, hospital infrastructure, innovation and, above all, collaboration.For Kerala, a state known for its strong healthcare ecosystem, the pandemic also created an opportunity to look beyond clinical care, towards the businesses, technologies, entrepreneurs and innovators building the future of healthcare.What began as an effort to create a common platform for the healthcare fraternity gradually evolved into a larger mission: to bring the entire healthcare ecosystem into one room.Doctors. Hospitals. Manufacturers. MSMEs. Startups. MedTech companies. Diagnostics companies. Digital health innovators. Investors. Academicians. Policymakers.Over the next five editions, the healthcare ecosystem grew and HOSPEX grew with it. The focus expanded beyond medical equipment to include AI, advanced diagnostics, digital healthcare, medical tourism, wellness, startups and emerging technologies.Over its first five editions, HOSPEX has brought together more than 500 exhibitors and 10,000 visitors, along with over 50 expert speakers and 100 workshops and sessions.Now entering its sixth edition from September 24 to 26 at Chakolas Pavilion Event Centre in Kochi, HOSPEX will focus on the theme ‘Future of Healthcare: Digital, Devices, Diagnostics, Medical Tourism and Wellness.’The 2026 edition showcases the healthcare sector preparing for its next phase, with dedicated programmes on AI in healthcare, smart clinical laboratories, biomedical engineering, healthcare procurement, future-ready healthcare facilities and medical tourism.But the future vision of HOSPEX extends beyond three days of exhibition and conferences. It is about creating a stronger ecosystem where doctors meet innovators, startups meet investors, hospitals discover new technologies, MSMEs find markets and Indian healthcare businesses build international connections.A vital catalyst in this ongoing journey has been the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises. MSME is supporting the HOSPEX healthcare expo and has been a crucial partner for the past 4 editions. By providing a strong framework for local manufacturers to showcase their innovations and by facilitating critical market access, MSME is actively helping the ecosystem grow and evolve, ensuring that smaller businesses can sustainably scale alongside larger healthcare entities.A vital catalyst in this ongoing journey has been the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises. It has to be built together.HOSPEX is led by a team of doctors and healthcare innovators:Dr Mithun Raju P, Dr Arun Krishna, Dr Nivin J S, Dr Indu Kandaga and Dr Achuth Ajith Kumar, bringing together clinical expertise, hospital leadership, patient safety, entrepreneurship and healthcare innovation, with the initiative also mentored and guided by Rama Venu Gopal.What began as an idea has become a community. And that community is now looking towards what healthcare can become next. One of the areas being explored is the Future Smart Hospital looking at how hospitals can become more connected, technology-enabled and patient-centric.

Article Title: SC asks EC to set timeline for resolving name, symbol dispute between TMC factions
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Thursday asked the Election Commission to decide at the earliest which of the two rival factions of the All India Trinamool Congress will get the party's name and symbol.Hearing a plea filed by Mamata Banerjee , the top court asked the poll panel to inform it by Monday when it expected to take a final decision on the dispute.The Supreme Court also referred to the Shiv Sena factional dispute and said the row between the two AITC factions should be decided expeditiously.The development comes days after the Election Commission temporarily allotted Mamata Banerjee's faction the name "Mamata All India Trinamool Congress" and the "football player" symbol.The rival faction was allotted the name "Democratic Trinamool Congress" and the "envelope" symbol.Earlier, in an interim order, the poll panel froze the All India Trinamool Congress name and its "flowers and grass" symbol after recognising a factional dispute within the party. Neither faction can use the original name or symbol until the dispute is finally settled.The temporary arrangement will apply to the upcoming bypolls, with candidates of the two factions contesting under the separate names and symbols allotted by the Commission.The Election Commission has been hearing competing claims over control of the party, its name and election symbol. Both sides have submitted documents and appeared before the Commission during the proceedings.The dispute reached the poll panel after rival groups staked claims to control the TMC. The commission subsequently sought submissions on issues including organisational control, authorised office-bearers, party assets, the party name and its election symbol.
Article Summary: The Supreme Court asked the Election Commission to decide at the earliest which of the two rival factions of the All India Trinamool Congress will get the party's name and symbol. The Election Commission has been hearing competing claims over control of the party, its name and election symbol.

Article Title: Gyanesh Kumar should be criminally prosecuted for 'treason': Priyanka Gandhi on SIR row
Article Text:
Cong MP Priyanka Gandhi targets EC over SIR, alleges 'voter roll tampering'.

'Electoral process completely tainted': Cong

'Justice will be served': Rahul

'All actions have been in accordance': EC

'All three Commissioners were unanimous': BJP

Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra on Thursday slammed the Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, alleging that he should be "criminally prosecuted" if found responsible for "tampering with electoral rolls and deleting voters' names. "Her remarks came a day after The Indian Express published a report claiming that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had formally raised objections at least 14 times over 10 months to decisions and orders related to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.Speaking to reporters in Wayanad, Kerala, Priyanka Gandhi said, "Anybody who plays around with the process, the democratic process of our elections is committing treason against this nation. That is our very clear stand. I do not think anybody in that position should have legal protection in the way that he has. The Chief Election Commissioner has. If they have done illegal acts because tampering with the voters' rolls, deleting, I believe, 13 crore voters is a criminal act against democracy, against the Constitution and against the nation. ""Since criminal acts fall under a particular law, and people are usually tried and prosecuted for doing those criminal acts, I do not see why the Election Commissioner has to have any protection against it," the Congress MP said."If he has done an illegal act, he has been fully aware that this is happening under his nose. His colleagues have brought it to his attention. He has ignored it and intentionally allowed an unfair election to take place. He should be criminally prosecuted just like any other criminal, and he should be tried for treason. This is my very clear stand," she added.Earlier on Wednesday, Priyanka Gandhi had also called the issue "an extremely serious" one for democracy."This is an extremely serious issue for our democracy. If there are no elections, then where is democracy? If elections are unfair and rigged in any manner, then the Election Commission is assisting in that. If the Election Commissioner is not only aware of it but also allowing it to happen, then it is a very serious assault on democracy. It is an act of treason," she said.Congress leader Jairam Ramesh also launched a fresh attack on Gyanesh Kumar , alleging irregularities in the ECINet software and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.Ramesh said a series of reports had raised serious questions over the functioning of the poll panel and alleged that the electoral process had been "completely compromised and tainted".He said, "Yesterday, sensational revelations in a major national daily brought to light that the CEC has completely undermined the integrity, reliability, and competence of the Election Commission. This morning, another report in this series has emerged."Ramesh alleged that Goa's chief electoral officer (CEO) wrote to the ECI eight times in seven days seeking the reinstatement of valid voters whose names had been removed by the ECINet software. He said Electoral Registration Officers (EROs) had confirmed that the voters were valid, but their emails were ignored and the names were removed.He also stated that the process for adding new voters through Form 6 had been made more difficult and claimed that Gen Z was being "deliberately targeted" to exclude young voters from electoral rolls.Ramesh said the latest allegations reinforced what leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi had been saying for nearly two years, referring to the results of the Haryana and Maharashtra assembly elections."The electoral process has been completely compromised and tainted. This is the implementation of the Method of Disenfranchising Indians (MODI) by Gyanesh Kumar," Ramesh said.He also called for the CEC's resignation, saying, "If there is even a shred of decency and ethics left in CEC Gyanesh Kumar, his first step should be to immediately resign from his position. After that, the Prime Minister and Home Minister will be held accountable for their nefarious designs."Congress leader Rahul Gandhi also took to X, stating that, "The enemies of the Constitution have been exposed. Justice will be served."Earlier on Wednesday, Rahul described "vote chori" as a "crime against the Indian people" and an attack on the Constitution.In a post on X, Rahul Gandhi said, "Vote chori is a crime against the Indian people and a direct attack on our constitution. The BJP, RSS and EC who organised it have committed an act of treason. Justice will be served."In a video, he also addressed the Election Commission and election officials, saying, "I am clearly telling the Election Commission and election officers: What you are doing is wrong. This is treason; it is against the nation. Do not forget this. The time will come! We will catch you! You will not be spared."According to the media report, Election Commissioners Sandhu and Joshi had objected at least 14 times to decisions taken in the Commission's name without their knowledge or approval. The reported objections covered issues including voter registration and deletion, changes to Form 6 and the handling of the electoral-roll database.The ECI rejected the suggestion that the reported objections amounted to a division within the Commission. ECI officials said all decisions, including those related to SIR, were taken unanimously with the approval of all three commissioners.In a statement, the poll panel said, "The ECI is a constitutional body that functions under the strict mandate of Article 324 of the Constitution, statutory rules and established institutional conventions. The Commission operates as a multi-member constitutional body. Written notes, observations, technical suggestions and internal checks-and-balances are standard, ongoing practices designed to ensure complete transparency, legal compliance and operational rigour. All actions of ECI have been in accordance with laws and instructions of the Commission. All official orders, decisions and administrative directions issued by the Commission carry full legal sanctions and follow established statutory procedures."The Commission further said, "Any operational queries or inputs raised by Commission members during draft stages are part of standard administrative practice aimed at safeguarding voter rights. The suggestions given by the Commissioners were for further improving the electoral processes," adding that differing views and observations were a normal part of institutional deliberations.BJP national spokesperson and MP Sambit Patra earlier defended the functioning of the Election Commission, saying discussions among the three commissioners were part of the democratic process."Look at the situation: if the three Election Commissioners do not communicate with each other, if there is no exchange of views or consultation, and they simply agree to everything, then the opposition parties claim it is a dictatorship. They say this government appointed these three commissioners; they just say yes. Now, there have been 14 instances of correspondence among the three of them, official deliberations, as far as we gather from the media. It is not as if the Bharatiya Janata Party goes and reads these letters; rather, reports in the media indicate that official deliberations took place among the three, which is a sign of a healthy democracy," he said."I would say that today, all the opposition parties have fallen into a trap, the trap of claiming that the Election Commission and the government were acting dictatorially. On the contrary, I would say this is pure democracy.Deliberations are taking place, and the Election Commission has stated very clearly in the very first paragraph of its document that, following all official democratic deliberations, the final outcome, the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), was achieved with unanimity," Patra said."In other words, all three Commissioners were unanimous; there was no difference of opinion or dissent among them," he added.Meanwhile, ECI sources maintained that all decisions taken by the poll panel, including those related to SIR, were unanimous and had the approval of both Election Commissioners and the Chief Election Commissioner.
Article Summary: Congress leader Jairam Ramesh also launched a fresh attack on Gyanesh Kumar, alleging irregularities in the ECINet software and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. He said a series of reports had raised serious questions over the functioning of the poll panel and alleged that the electoral process had been "completely compromised"

Article Title: Tamil Nadu Pocso case: Businessman Veeramani, aide arrested; what we know so far
Article Text:
Child rape: Granite baron Veeramani’s premises raided

What is the Veeramani case?

Case takes political turn

Summons issued to officials

NEW DELHI: The Central Crime Branch (CCB) has arrested Ganesan, a longtime aide of granite businessman and Gem Granites chief Veeramani, in connection with a POCSO case involving the alleged sexual abuse of minor girls.Ganesan is the fourth accused arrested in the case. Police said he had worked with Veeramani’s Gem Granites for 23 years and is currently employed with Balaji Global Enterprises.According to investigators, Ganesan had video clips on his mobile phone that purportedly showed Veeramani in an obscene act involving a minor girl. Police said he did not inform the authorities about the videos.The CCB is now investigating how Ganesan came to possess the clips and why he allegedly kept them without alerting police. Investigators are also examining his mobile phone to determine whether any data was deleted.Veeramani was arrested on August 29 along with two alleged accomplices after the Anti-Vice Squad (AVS) registered a case over the alleged rape of minor girls. The three accused were subsequently remanded in Puzhal Central Prison.Police said the case came to light after a USB drive containing a video clip purportedly showing Veeramani sexually assaulting a juvenile girl was recovered.Investigators identified the survivor and established that she was a minor when the alleged offence took place in 2019.The video was also examined as part of the investigation into the allegations against Veeramani.The investigation has also expanded to suspected financial transactions allegedly made to influence the earlier probe, police said.Investigators are examining bank transactions and the possible involvement of intermediaries in the movement of funds.The ruling TVK on Wednesday demanded that DMK president MK Stalin explain how the POCSO case involving Veeramani was handled when the DMK was in power, alleging that the investigation was allowed to weaken and questioning why a final report was filed.The TVK alleged that the case had been “buried”. The party also questioned former law minister S. Regupathy over his handling of video footage submitted in connection with the case.“Under whose pressure did the then Law Minister Regupathy allow the investigation to be weakened? What was the reason?” the TVK asked.The party also sought an explanation for the filing of the final report, alleging that it was submitted without a proper investigation.Chennai Central Crime Branch police have issued summons to Assistant Commissioner Yasmin and Anti-Vice Squad inspectors Mahesh Kumar and Rajalakshmi in connection with the sexual assault case against industrialist Veeramani.The three officials, who had earlier investigated and closed the case, have been asked to appear in person for an inquiry and provide their explanations, Chennai Police said.
Article Summary: Ganesan is the fourth accused arrested in the case. Ganesan had video clips on his mobile phone that purportedly showed Veeramani in an obscene act involving a minor girl. Police said he did not inform the authorities about the videos. The investigation has also expanded to suspected financial transactions allegedly made to influence the earlier probe.

Article Title: 6 Ukrainians accused of training armed rebels in India, Myanmar get default bail
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: An NIA court in Delhi Wednesday granted bail to six Ukrainian nationals arrested in March this year for allegedly running a training camp for ethnic armed rebels in India and Myanmar.The court, which ordered their release on a cash bond of Rs 1 lakh each, also discharged them from offences under the Immigration and Foreigners Act following after the Foreigners Regional Registration Office (FRRO), which deals with the immigration matters involving foreign nationals, settled the offences on payment of a penalty of Rs 5.5 lakh each.The offences, which pertained to illegal entry and visa violations, are compoundable at the level of the FRRO.Special judge Prashant Sharma granted them default bail on grounds of parity with their American co-accused Matthew Aaron Van Dyke.While granting bail to Dyke on Sept 18, the judge had dismissed the NIA’s opposition, observing that even if the probe was far from over, “at this stage it cannot be concluded that applicant/ accused Matthew Aaron Vandyke is not entitled for default bail”.Default bail is provisioned in the UAPA if the probe agency doesn’t file charge sheet containing offences under the anti-terror law with 180 days of arresting the accused. Following this, the court had directed that the other six accused could also seek default bail.Earlier this month, the agency filed a charge sheet which did not mention provisions of the UAPA, 1967, which was invoked in the initial FIR.
Article Summary: Six Ukrainian nationals arrested in March this year for allegedly running a training camp for ethnic armed rebels in India and Myanmar. The court discharged them from offences under the Immigration and Foreigners Act. The Foreigners Regional Registration Office (FRRO) settled the offences on payment of a penalty of Rs 5.5 lakh each.

Article Title: At 18, Salman Khan lost his father, drove taxi for months before becoming an Army man and now an Asian Games rowing medallist
Article Text:
Indian rowers Satnam Singh and Salman Khan pose with their bronze medal (PTI Photo)

Salman lost his father at 18

A friend's advice changed his life

How Salman became a rower

The turning point

From national gold to international success

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

From driving a cab to wearing the India jersey

For rower Salman Khan , winning an Asian Games medal is the latest chapter in a journey that began with family responsibilities, financial struggles and a job as a cab driver.The Indian rower won the bronze medal in the men's double sculls event alongside teammate Satnam Singh at the Asian Games 2026 on Thursday. The Indian pair stayed in second place until the 1,500m mark before slipping to third in the final 500m. They finished the race in 6:13.25 at the Nagaragawa International Regatta Course.China's Yi Xudi and Yide Nie won gold with a timing of 6:09.37, while Uzbekistan's Pavel Sorin and Mekhrojbek Mamatkulov took silver in 6:10.49.For Salman, the medal has come after years of hard work and a life that could have taken a very different path.Salman was born in Pure Dhingai in Amethi district of Uttar Pradesh. His father, Mohammed Kasim Khan, worked in truck-body construction in Tauru, Haryana, where Salman completed his schooling.He was the eldest of four brothers and two sisters. When his father died of dengue, Salman was just 18 years old.With his younger siblings still studying, the responsibility of supporting the family fell on him. His dream of joining the Army had to take a backseat as earning a livelihood became his priority.Salman started driving an Uber cab in Delhi. He worked day and night to keep his family going.Salman had not given up completely on his Army dream. One day, while resting after a shift, a close friend reminded him that his height and physical build could help him in the Army. That advice pushed him to try again.He handed over the cab to another driver and spent four months preparing through hard running and training. He cleared the recruitment rally, medical and written examinations.In September 2018, he joined the Bombay Engineer Group (BEG), Kirkee, Pune.At the training centre, coaches noticed Salman's height and physique and introduced him to rowing. He knew nothing about the sport and initially had no interest in taking it up. With his family's financial situation, sport was not something he thought he could pursue.He refused several times. But the coaches continued to push him and eventually put him in a boat. They saw potential in him and began training him seriously.Salman's first inter-centre regatta gave him the first sign that he could make something out of rowing. He won a silver medal, which gave him confidence.The next major step came in 2021 when Salman cleared the ergometer benchmarks and was selected for the Army Rowing Node at CME Pune. Training alongside some of India's best rowers changed his outlook.What had started as a sport he did not even want to take up became something he wanted to pursue professionally.Salman began to believe that rowing could help him win medals for India.Salman's progress continued over the next few years. At the 36th National Games in Gujarat in 2022, he won gold. At the 2023 Senior Nationals, he won gold in the single sculls against Olympian Dattu Bhokanal. That performance helped him earn a place in the India camp.In 2024, Salman won his first international gold at the Asian Rowing Cup in South Korea with Nitin Deol. That victory also earned him a promotion to Naib Subedar in the Indian Army.He followed it with a silver at the 2025 Australian Rowing Championships and another silver at the 2025 Asian Rowing Championships.Those performances helped him secure his place in India's Asian Games squad.For Salman, representing India carries a special meaning because of where his journey started. He came from a village background and had to take responsibility for his family at a very young age.His mother, Jabrun Nisha, remained a major source of strength for him, while his wife, Sahiba Khatoon, supported him throughout his journey.His coaches and support staff also played a major role in keeping him on the rowing path, particularly during periods when he lost interest in the sport.At the Army Rowing Node, officers and coaches helped him regain his focus and develop as an athlete.Salman's journey from Amethi to the Indian Army, and from an unfamiliar boat to an Asian Games medal, has been built over years of perseverance, discipline and the support of his family, coaches and teammates.
Article Summary: Salman Khan won a bronze medal in the men's double sculls at the Asian Games 2026 on Thursday. The Indian pair stayed in second place until the 1,500m mark before slipping to third in the final 500m. China's Yi Xudi and Yide Nie won gold with a timing of 6:09.37, while Uzbekistan's Pavel Sorin and Mekhrojbek Mamatkulov took silver.

Article Title: NSE IPO: Stock lists at Rs 1,800 versus issue price of Rs 1,785 on BSE with 0.8% premium; check details
Article Text:
Before the IPO opened for subscription, NSE had raised Rs 6,746 crore from more than 150 anchor investors.

NSE Debuts on BSE, MSEI

NSE IPO GMP

NSE IPO listing date today: National Stock Exchange of India ’s shares debuted on the Bombay Stock Exchange at Rs 1,800 versus an issue price of Rs 1,785, marking a premium of around 0.8%.NSE made its stock market debut with a market capitalisation of more than Rs 4.45 lakh crore, becoming the second listed stock exchange in India. Its valuation at listing was significantly higher than that of rival BSE, whose current market capitalisation stands at Rs 1.33 lakh crore.Market participants were tracking grey market movements closely ahead of the listing, which is among the most anticipated market debuts of the year so far. Analysts said restrictions on exits by most large shareholders could limit the availability of NSE shares in the near term, potentially putting upward pressure on prices at a later stage.NSE's market debut gives investors an opportunity to assess how the exchange should be valued. Its longer-term growth outlook helped attract strong institutional interest, while retail investors appeared more cautious amid concerns about derivatives volumes, regulatory pressures and the possibility of more shares entering the market.Although investors remain broadly positive on NSE's longer-term prospects, the stock's performance in the months following its listing could depend on the amount of additional equity that becomes available once the lock-in periods for existing shareholders come to an end.In a circular issued on Wednesday, MSE said NSE's equity shares would be admitted for trading on its capital market segment under the ‘Permitted to trade’ category, effective September 24.The Metropolitan Stock Exchange is a Sebi-recognised national stock exchange that operates an electronic trading platform covering capital markets, equity derivatives, currency derivatives and debt segments. Its platform includes equity and index derivatives, debt and currency derivatives, with more than 250 listings and over 3,100 companies available for trading.The development comes days after NSE MD and CEO Ashish Chauhan made it clear that the exchange would not approach Sebi for permission to trade its own shares on its platform. Existing regulations of the market regulator do not permit a recognised stock exchange to list its own securities on its own trading platform.In the unlisted market, traders saw a grey market premium or GMP of around 2.2%. The stock has listed on a waek note with less than 1% premium over its issue price.The GMP was much higher earlier at Rs 250-310 a share, or roughly 14-17%. The steep decline had suggested expectations of only modest gains when the shares list."While investors have been waiting for the NSE listing for long, the enthusiasm has moderated because of the large issue size and expected supply," Abhay Doshi, co-founder of UnlistedArena.com told ET.At the IPO's upper price of Rs 1,785 per share, NSE's valuation stands at Rs 4.42 lakh crore, compared with Rs 1.33 lakh crore for rival BSE. Some market participants said the balance between available supply and investor demand could play an important role in determining how NSE shares perform in the initial trading sessions after listing.The listing brings to an end NSE's long-running journey towards becoming a listed company and make it India's second listed stock exchange after BSE.NSE launched its initial public offering earlier this month, seeking to raise Rs 22,562 crore through a 12.64 crore-share offer for sale (OFS) by existing shareholders.Since the issue was entirely an OFS, NSE itself will not receive any money from the IPO. The proceeds will instead accrue to the shareholders selling their stakes through the offering.The IPO price band was fixed at Rs 1,700 to Rs 1,785 per share. With the lot size set at 8 shares, retail investors were required to invest a minimum of Rs 14,280 to apply for the issue.Before the IPO opened for subscription, NSE had raised Rs 6,746 crore from more than 150 anchor investors.Foreign portfolio investors made up Rs 2,883 crore, or 43%, of the total anchor book. The anchor round saw participation from more than 20 foreign long-only funds, including Singapore sovereign wealth fund GIC, Abu Dhabi Investment Authority and Norges Bank.Domestic institutional participation was similarly spread across investors. More than 25 mutual funds, along with 11 insurance and pension companies, invested around Rs 3,588 crore, accounting for 53% of the anchor book.LIC, which is NSE's largest shareholder with a 10.72% stake, also participated in the anchor round. LIC, LIC Mutual Fund and LIC Pension Fund together invested more than Rs 500 crore. The investment was made even though LIC's existing shareholding in NSE is larger than the stake being offered through the IPO.The SBI group also took part in the anchor book through SBI Mutual Fund, SBI General, SBI Life and SBI Pension Fund. State Bank of India and SBI Capital Markets are together selling a 1% stake in NSE, while the group's combined investment in the exchange through its various entities exceeds Rs 400 crore.NSE's first public issue attracted strong demand during the three-day subscription period from September 17 to September 21. The IPO was subscribed nearly six times the shares on offer. Qualified institutional buyers (QIBs) drove the demand, subscribing to their reserved portion around 13 times, while the portions allocated to retail investors and non-institutional investors (NII) were subscribed 1.4 times and 6.6 times, respectively.
Article Summary: NSE made its stock market debut with a market capitalisation of more than Rs 4.45 lakh crore, becoming the second listed stock exchange in India. Its valuation at listing was significantly higher than that of rival BSE, whose current market cap stands at Rs 1.33 lakh crore. Analysts said restrictions on exits by most large shareholders could limit the availability of NSE shares.

Article Title: After split verdict, SC refers law on EC appointment to larger bench; decision comes amid row over EC functioning
Article Text:

SC: Constitution bench should deal with case to prevent delay

NEW DELHI: On a day when Election Commission found itself under the scanner, a two-judge bench of Supreme Court gave a split verdict on whether the issue of validity of the law on appointment of CEC/ECs be referred to a constitution bench, but later agreed to refer the case to a larger bench for the sake of early adjudication of the contentious issue.Validity of several provisions of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023 has been challenged on the ground that the law gives the executive "overwhelming" power to appoint its nominee as election commissioner, as the selection panel composed of the PM, a Cabinet minister and the leader of the opposition is designed to give govt a 2:1 majority. The petitioners contended that EC's independence would be compromised in this process.The 2023 law was framed to replace an SC verdict which had directed that selection be done by a committee of the PM, CJI and leader of the opposition until Parliament determined the composition by passing a law. "Speaking in one voice would have better served institutional cohesion. Unfortunately, the court is divided in its opinion," a bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and S C Sharma said.The hearing in the case went on for five days and at the fag end of proceedings, the Centre had sought referral of the case to a constitution bench.Noting that appointment of CEC/ECs was being litigated for last 11 years in SC after a petition was filed in 2015, the bench decided that the case should not be referred to a three-judge bench, which is the normal procedure, but to a constitution bench to settle the issue once and for all. It reasoned that a decision by a three-judge bench would be of little worth and only delay adjudication of the significant issue(s) that these writ petitions raise."Thus, we direct that the papers be placed before the CJI for considering the desirability of constituting a constitution bench of such number of judges to decide the question of vires of Sec 7 and the other provisions of Act," the bench said.The bench expressed hope that the case would be given priority as the issues raised were of "foundational importance to the democratic fabric of the country and its citizenry"."Petitioners seem to be justified in expressing their anxiety that references to five-judge benches remain unresolved for years. If statistics are any guide, none can say with any reasonable degree of certainty when long-pending references will get resolved. Undisputedly, this is an area of grave concern and the inordinate delay in resolution of the references is itself a source of institutional embarrassment which all stakeholders ought to strive to avoid. Self-introspection, indeed, is required," it said."We, thus, take this opportunity of requesting the Chief Justice to also explore the necessity of constituting a permanent five-judge bench to decide pure constitutional issues. This is not something novel that we are saying. It has been opined time and again by responsible citizens and we simply endorse their opinion. Given that resolving constitutional issues is the primary task of judges of this court, that must remain its core priority.Pendency of references for far too long, any period between five and 20 years or more, does not reflect well on the institution. It is time that the institution addresses the issue with the urgency and promptitude it deserves," the bench said.
Article Summary: Supreme Court gave a split verdict on whether the issue of validity of the law on appointment of CEC/ECs be referred to a constitution bench. The two-judge bench agreed to refer the case to a larger bench for the sake of early adjudication of the contentious issue.

Article Title: SIR queries raised, but pertained to draft stage; focusing on some notes while ignoring others gives only one part of picture: EC

Dr. Sukhbir Singh Sandhu, Gyanesh Kumar, Dr. Vivek Joshi

NEW DELHI: Faced with criticism for election commissioners S S Sandhu and Vivek Joshi being cut out of crucial decisions, the Election Commission on Wednesday said the “operational queries, inputs and suggestions” raised over the past 10 months by the two commissioners, including on the special intensive revision (SIR) process, remained limited to the draft stages and were part of the standard administrative practice and decision-making process at the Commission.All decisions taken by the commission in the past one year, including SIR, “are an outcome of the unanimous decisions of the full commission,” EC asserted in a statement rebutting the contention that the chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar was acting unilaterally.EC was reacting to a report in Indian Express claiming that the two election commissioners had objected to steps taken by the poll panel on 14 occasions over 10 months, including the changes made to Form 6 as part of SIR, restricting field officers’ access to electoral roll databases and even regarding postings and foreign tours involving EC personnel.Sandhu and Joshi even wrote to the Cabinet secretary separately on July 29, complaining about redistribution of work by the senior deputy election commissioner (DEC) in charge of administration EC and the resultant centralisation of decision -making , said the report.In its statement, EC said that differing views and observations are a normal part of deliberation in any institution before a final decision is taken.“Written notes, observations, technical suggestions and internal checks and balances are standard, ongoing practices to ensure transparency, legal compliance and operational rigour." EC said all its actions as well as official orders, decisions and administrative decisions have been in accordance with laws and commission's instructions and carry full legal sanction."Highlighting certain specific internal notes/observations spread over the period of 10 months while overlooking the much larger body of approvals, decisions, instructions and initiatives give only one part of the picture," EC said adding that its decisions, instructions, 40 new initiatives and conduct of polls in six states/UTs in the past one year were all based on unanimous decisions by the commission in the past one year.Sources in EC said the objections were largely raised in written notes sent by the election commissioners to the deputy election commissioners (DECs), in many cases after they had signed on the concerned file following a unanimous decision; including in the cases of changes made to Form 6. The two commissioners, Joshi in May and Sandhu in August, had argued that changes in Form 6 could be carried out only by the government. However, sources maintained, after they along with the CEC unanimously approved the file relating to SIR orders for Bihar (Phase 1) and then a dozen states (Phase 2), which listed the revised Form 6 and the accompanying declaration on citizenship. In fact, by the time Sandhu objected, the Supreme Court had already upheld the validity of SIR as well as the processes followed by EC, sources said.As part of his case against powers getting centralised and CEC not taking his two colleagues in confidence, Sandhu had raised the issue of who had authorised filing of appeals on EC's behalf before the SIR tribunals in West Bengal. Sources, however, told TOI that this was as per the Supreme Court order dated April 1, 2026, particularly para 9 that stated that appeals may be filed by "persons whose names have been excluded from the voters list" or "by the authorities of the ECI, who may be aggrieved by the inclusion of names by the adjudicatory authorities".On the commissioners’ alleged objection to centralisation of the electoral roll database or ERONet/ECINet, allegedly with restricted access to field officers like the electoral registration officers (EROs) to decide on addition of deletion of names, the Commission said digital platforms such as ECINet operate under strict data security protocols to prevent unauthorised tampering, manipulation, etc. "IT security checks and audit controls are standard cybersecurity measures implemented across national databases. Statutory authorities, including EROs and district election officers (DEOs), function as per statutory powers for registration and deletion under law,” said EC. Sources in EC told TOI that while EROs and DEOs may have faced access issues due to system errors on some occasions, they have full access to electors databases and have been deciding on roll updations during SIR.Sources in the Commission did not contest Joshi's claim that agenda and minutes of EC meetings were not being circulated, but said this has been the norm before the present commission assumed office.Responding to the objections to decision of the DEC (Administration) to change the officer in charge of IT division, sources said that powers to decide appointment, recruitment, transfers and postings of officers above the level of section officer and posting and transfer of personal staff of election commissioners and DECs were delegated to DEC (Administration) in 1997.Regarding Joshi's April 16 objection to EC officers being sent on foreign trips without the "commission's" approval, sources said the power in this regard has been with the CEC since long.Reacting to Sandhu's objection that he had learnt of EC's new IT modules, portals etc from the media, sources pointed that both Sandhu and Joshi were present at ECINet's launch on January 22.
Article Summary: The Election Commission has been criticised for cutting out two election commissioners from crucial decisions. The two commissioners objected to steps taken by the poll panel on 14 occasions over 10 months. The objections were largely raised in written notes sent by the election commissioners to the deputy election commissioners.

NEW DELHI: Deliberating on the validity of the law on appointment of chief election commissioner and election commissioners by a panel of the PM, a cabinet minister and the leader of opposition, Justice Dipankar Datta on Wednesday pointed out drawbacks and said it gave "overwhelming" power to the executive and made the presence of the LoP "ornamental", undermining the appearance of independence in the selection process. He also noted that since independence, govts had tried to control the poll body."Over seven decades, every dispensation wresting office found it convenient to keep institutions which the Constitution envisioned to be independent under their control. To enact a law on the lines empowered by Article 324(2) would have meant freeing the ECI from exclusive executive control and inviting trouble for the ruling regime. To the mind of this court, this has not been the failing of any one party or one period. A consistent trait of political power, discernible over the decades, has been to preserve leverage over the very body that is meant to judge its claim to power," Justice Datta said.He said if free and fair elections were to be ensured, it was axiomatic that the EC must not only be an independent body but also be seen to act independently and it was "painful to note that not a single party in power, entrusted by the people of India to govern this great nation", took the initiative of enacting a law of the nature which Article 324(2) left to the supreme law-making body, ie Parliament, to legislate.Also read: SC refers law on EC appointment to larger bench; decision comes amid row over EC functioning "Placing its own electoral fortunes in the hands of a truly independent arbiter was not favoured by any political party, for obvious reasons. To remain in power, the consistent pursuit through executive action has indeed been simple - influence the composition of the EC, control the process of appointment of CEC and ECs and, thereby, temper adverse electoral outcomes," Justice Datta said.Summarising the contentions raised against the law, he added, "The bottom line of the argument runs thus: it would not be a fallacious metaphor if it is said that since the umpire is picked by the captain of one side in a cricket match and his team wins, even if the decisions taken by such umpire are correct, it has the patina of suspicion, for, at the end of the day, the umpire has effectively been chosen by the winning captain. "Justice Datta further said, "There can be no gainsaying that free and fair elections, to a large extent, depend on a truly independent EC. It is not enough for the EC to be independent, it must also appear to be independent. The minister nominated by the prime minister, to function as the third member on the selection committee chaired by the prime minister, cannot be expected to defy his own nominator. In such a circumstance, the inclusion of a minister in the selection committee fails to provide the independent counterweight that a neutral selector could and he would merely echo the voice of his leader; and, consequently, the presence of the leader of opposition in the selection committee becomes largely ornamental, without furthering the purpose of his inclusion. "
Article Summary: Justice Dipankar Datta said the law gave "overwhelming" power to the executive. He also noted that since independence, govts had tried to control the poll body. He said it was axiomatic that the EC must not only be an independent body but also be seen to act independently.

NEW DELHI: The BJP is set to have the numbers on its side in the upcoming Rajya Sabha elections in Uttar Pradesh, with the party-led alliance expected to win eight of the 10 seats going to polls in the state. A candidate needs around 37 votes to win a Rajya Sabha seat.The BJP can comfortably win seven seats, while the SP-Congress combine can secure two.The contest for the 10th seat could be closer, with the BJP-led alliance starting with around 31 votes against around 29 for the SP-Congress side.The polls could also mark the end of the BSP's representation in Parliament. It became vacant earlier this month after Sharma resigned from the Rajya Sabha following his appointment as lieutenant governor of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.The BSP had managed to retain its Rajya Sabha presence in 2020 after the BJP fielded only eight candidates for 10 seats. Article Title: EC faultlines have a long history, dating back to 1989
Article Text:
Election Commission of India

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: It is not the first time that the fault lines within the Election Commission are out in the open. The trend started from the time it became a multi-member body in 1989.Two election commissioners S S Dhanoa and V S Seigell were appointed in October 1989 and joined the poll body then led by chief election commissioner (CEC) R V S Peri Sastri. Though Sastri never publicly spoke about it, it is widely believed that the new arrangement was perceived by him as a dilution in power. By January 1990, the appointment of the two commissioners was rescinded and the EC reverted to being a single—member body.In 1993, with T N Seshan as an all-powerful CEC, the commission was once again made a multi-member body with the appointment of election commissioners M S Gill and G V G Krishnamurthy. What followed was a running feud between Seshan on the one hand and Gill and Krishnamurthy on the other. Seshan viewed the appointments as a direct assault on the independence of his office and completely refused to recognize the two new commissioners. He refused to share official documents with Gill and Krishnamurthy, barred them from attending critical meetings, and would not allocate them any office work. He openly ridiculed the election commissioners in interviews, even referring to them as “two donkeys in my office”.Interestingly, it was on Seshan’s plea challenging the govt’s decision to make EC a multi-member body that the Supreme Court had, in 1995, ruled that the election commissioners and CEC were equal in status, power and decision-making authority and that the CEC was only “first among equals”.The other internal feud in EC to recall would be one between then CEC N Gopalaswami and election commissioner Navin Chawla between 2006 and 2009. Months before he was to step down upon the end of his tenure, Gopalaswami wrote to the President of India recommending the removal of Chawla on grounds of a pro-Congress bias. In his note to the President, Gopalaswami alleged that Chawla was passing on details of EC’s meetings to senior Congress leaders, often taking “toilet breaks” during commission meetings to do so. Gopalaswami’s recommendation was however turned down by the Manmohan Singh govt and Chawla succeeded him as CEC.During the 2019 general election, the differences between then CEC Sunil Arora and then election commissioner Ashok Lavasa came to the fore, with media reports alleging that he had dissented in cases relating to complaints of alleged model code of conduct violations by Prime Minister Narendra Modi and then BJP president Amit Shah, but was overruled without the commission making his dissent noted public. EC put out a clarification that dissent notes were only made public in quasi-judicial orders passed by EC.Lavasa resigned on August 18, 2020, two years short of his tenure, and joined the Manila-headquartered Asian Development Bank (ADB) as its Vice-President.Arun Goyal was the last election commissioner to quit in the middle of his term. Though he had cited personal reasons in his resignation dated March 9, 2024, it was widely speculated that he was not on the best of terms with the then chief election commissioner Rajiv Kumar.
Article Summary: The fault lines within the Election Commission are out in the open. The trend started from the time it became a multi-member body in 1989. The other internal feud in EC to recall would be one between then CEC N Gopalaswami and election commissioner Navin Chawla.

Article Title: India's proposal under consideration for safe Black Sea shipping, Zelenskyy says

India has emerged as one of the countries whose proposals are being considered for restoring safe commercial shipping in the Black Sea, with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy saying Egypt, India and Turkey have outlined options for a maritime truce between Russia and Ukraine.Speaking to leaders at the United Nations on Wednesday, Zelenskyy said Ukraine was ready to support a maritime truce based on the proposals and that Russia now needed to respond.“We are waiting for Russia's response. Ukraine is ready ... to ensure safe shipping and food security in the Black Sea if Russia is ready to take real steps towards de-escalation too. We have to start somewhere,” Zelenskyy said.The remarks came at Ukraine's Crimean Platform summit on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly, ahead of a UN Security Council meeting on Russia's war in Ukraine.The reference to India's role comes amid New Delhi's efforts to remain engaged with both Moscow and Kyiv and encourage an end to the conflict.External affairs minister S Jaishankar said earlier this month that India had been in continuous touch with both Ukraine and Russia and was exploring ideas that could contribute to mitigating and eventually ending the war.“What we are trying to do is to see if there are ideas and suggestions which can be developed in some way in which they will contribute to the mitigation, ideally, the cessation of the conflict,” Jaishankar said during his visit to Warsaw.Jaishankar has also said India's position is that the conflict should end through dialogue and diplomacy.During his visit to Kyiv earlier this month, he met Zelenskyy and Ukrainian foreign minister Andrii Sybiha, with discussions including possible approaches to ending the conflict.“If India can be of any help, in any manner, we are there,” Jaishankar said in Kyiv.According to Reuters, Zelenskyy said Egypt, India and Turkey had proposed options to restore safe navigation for merchant vessels in the Black Sea, where cargo movements have been severely disrupted by attacks on ships and port infrastructure by both sides.Ukraine has been seeking ceasefires covering attacks on energy infrastructure as well as shipping in the Black Sea. Kyiv has also expressed concern that Russia could target power and heating facilities with missiles and drones during the winter.The disruption has also affected countries dependent on grain supplies from the Black Sea region. Reuters reported that wheat importers in Asia, the Middle East and Africa have faced difficulties securing supplies, while global wheat prices have risen.Zelenskyy said Ukraine was ready to ensure safe shipping and food security if Russia was prepared to take steps towards de-escalation.US secretary of state Marco Rubio said after meeting Russian foreign minister Sergei Lavrov on Wednesday that both Russia and Ukraine had expressed interest in a limited ceasefire involving grain and energy.The Kremlin has not publicly backed the proposals.Ahead of the Rubio-Lavrov meeting, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said there were currently no grounds for broader peace talks, while maintaining that Russia remained open to negotiations.“For now, there are no prerequisites for moving on to a peaceful negotiating track, although we, as the Russian side, remain open to peace talks,” Peskov said.Zelenskyy also said he was ready to meet Russian President Vladimir Putin at a trilateral meeting with US President Donald Trump.The latest developments come as India continues its diplomatic engagement with both sides.Jaishankar met US secretary of state Marco Rubio on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly on Wednesday and discussed the Ukraine situation, as well as India's concerns over the US Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act.

Article Title: Painkillers for every ache? CDSCO warns of kidney risks, antibiotic misuse
Article Text:
CDSCO warns against misuse of painkillers, antibiotics over kidney disease risk. (Photo: ANI)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Taking painkillers repeatedly for everyday aches or antibiotics without proper medical advice could put people at risk of kidney complications and other adverse effects, prompting the Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO) to issue a fresh advisory on their rational use.The drug regulator has asked people not to take non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), commonly used as painkillers, repeatedly or for prolonged periods without medical advice. It has also cautioned against self-medication with antibiotics and advised people with existing kidney disease or other risk factors for renal impairment to inform their doctor before taking NSAIDs.Prof Sandeep Mahajan, nephrologist at AIIMS, said that unregulated and prolonged use of painkillers can accelerate the decline in kidney function, particularly in people with chronic kidney disease. “All prescription medicines should be taken under the supervision of a qualified physician, with the prescribed dose and duration strictly followed. Medicines from alternative systems should also be used with caution, as some may contain substances that can be toxic to the kidneys. ”“Misuse of non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs can cause serious kidney injury, particularly in people with pre-existing kidney disease.Even short-term use can be risky in vulnerable individuals,” said Dr Dinesh Khullar, Group Chairman, Nephrology & Renal Transplant Medicine, Max Super Speciality Hospital, Saket. “People should therefore avoid unnecessary self-medication and take these medicines only on medical advice. ”The warning comes against the backdrop of a substantial chronic kidney disease burden in India. A 2025 systematic review of community-based studies estimated pooled chronic kidney disease prevalence at 13.24%, although estimates varied widely across regions and studies.The CDSCO circular, issued on Monday, says NSAIDs and antibiotics are prescription medicines under the Drugs and Cosmetics Rules and should be used only when clinically indicated, at the appropriate dose and duration and under medical supervision.The regulator has advised doctors to use the lowest effective dose of NSAIDs for the shortest appropriate duration, with extra caution in patients at risk of kidney injury. It has also urged judicious antibiotic use, avoiding unnecessary combinations, incorrect dosing and prolonged treatment.The National Centre for Disease Control's 2024 surveillance across 66 tertiary-care institutions found excessive consumption of “Watch” antibiotics, which have a higher resistance potential, along with inadequate use of “Access” antibiotics recommended as first-line treatment. The report also flagged inconsistent implementation of antimicrobial stewardship programmes.Self-medication remains common in India, with analgesics, antipyretics and antibiotics among the frequently self-medicated drugs. Pharmacists and retailers have been asked to enforce prescription rules, while hospitals and state regulators have been told to strengthen oversight and awareness of the risks, including kidney complications and antimicrobial resistance.
Article Summary: Drug regulator warns against misuse of painkillers, antibiotics over kidney disease risk. Self-medication remains common in India, with analgesics, antipyretics and antibiotics among the frequently self-medicated drugs. A 2025 systematic review of community-based studies estimated pooled chronic kidney disease prevalence at 13.24%.

Article Title: EC 'dissent' row: Opposition seeks CEC's arrest, fresh polls in states; BJP lauds 'pure democracy' - top developments
Article Text:
SIR row explodes into political confrontation as Opposition demands action against CEC

Opposition demands CEC's removal, arrest

Fresh polls demanded in Bihar, West Bengal

Akhilesh, Omar question EC functioning

BJP says EC differences show ‘pure democracy’

EC says all decisions were unanimous

NEW DELHI: The reported objections raised by two Election Commissioners to decisions linked to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls triggered a major political confrontation on Wednesday, with opposition parties demanding action against chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, an immediate halt to the SIR exercise and fresh elections in states where polls have already been held.The ruling BJP, however, defended the Election Commission, saying differences expressed by Election Commissioners during internal deliberations showed that the poll panel was functioning democratically rather than under a “dictatorial” system.The political row followed a media report which said Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had raised objections at least 14 times over 10 months to decisions and orders related to the SIR process and electoral rolls.The Election Commission has rejected the suggestion that the reported objections indicated a breakdown in its functioning.It said differing views and observations were a normal part of institutional deliberations and maintained that its decisions, including those concerning SIR, had been taken unanimously.Opposition parties, which have been criticising the EC over the SIR exercise, seized on the report to renew their demands for action against Gyanesh Kumar.Congress leader Rahul Gandhi reiterated his “vote chori” allegation against the Election Commission, describing it as “a crime against the people of India” and an attack on the Constitution.“The BJP, RSS and EC who organised it have committed an act of treason. Justice will be served,” Rae Bareli MP said.Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge said 73 Opposition Rajya Sabha MPs had submitted a fresh notice on April 24, seeking Kumar's removal.He questioned whether the Rajya Sabha chairman would decide on the pending notice since the Monsoon Session of Parliament had not yet been prorogued.Shiv Sena (UBT) chief Uddhav Thackeray and AAP national convenor Arvind Kejriwal went further, demanding that Kumar be removed and arrested.“Gyanesh Kumar should be immediately sacked and jailed,” Thackeray said.He also demanded that the last elections in Maharashtra, West Bengal and Tamil Nadu be nullified and fresh polls held in the three states using ballot papers.Kejriwal demanded that the entire SIR exercise be cancelled, all changes made under it be reversed and the voter list from three years ago be restored. He also called for Kumar's arrest and registration of a sedition case against him.TMC MP Derek O'Brien said, “Impeach CEC to save democracy.”Former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee also demanded Kumar's arrest and said he had “no moral authority to continue”.“This is such a scandalous story. We had never seen this in our lives. This Election Commissioner must be arrested. He has no moral authority to continue, and the BJP must see that they cannot destroy our Constitution. They cannot demolish democracy,” Banerjee said.The Opposition's demands also extended to fresh elections in states where polls have already taken place.RJD leader and Bihar leader of opposition Tejashwi Yadav demanded fresh elections in Bihar and West Bengal, alleging that the electoral mandates in the two states had been compromised through electoral fraud and institutional manipulation.“The opposition did not lose elections on the ground; the results were orchestrated by PM Modi and Amit Shah. In 2020, we were defeated through manipulation, and the same script was executed in 2025. Voter lists were purged, money was distributed, and counting was manipulated. The electoral outcomes in Bihar and Bengal are fraudulent, and we demand that fresh, transparent elections be held,” he said.Yadav also questioned changes to the rules governing the preservation of voting and counting records, alleging that the period had been reduced from one year to 45 days.He said this could make it difficult for parties to approach courts without access to election-related evidence.DMK president M K Stalin demanded Kumar's resignation and an immediate halt to the SIR exercise. He also sought a fair probe “into everything that transpired within the EC and those responsible should be held accountable”, according to news agency PTI.Stalin alleged that the report had raised doubts about the results of Assembly elections held after the SIR exercise and said his party had consistently opposed the deletion of voters from electoral rolls in the name of SIR.Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav said governments formed during a period when the Election Commission was not functioning impartially were “unconstitutional”.“This means that the governments which have been formed during this period are unconstitutional governments,” Yadav said.He alleged that interference in the poll panel amounted to “trampling” democracy and urged the Supreme Court to take suo motu cognisance of the matter.Jammu and Kashmir chief minister Omar Abdullah said the Centre and the Election Commission needed to take corrective steps to prevent people from losing faith in elections.“Corrective action needs to be taken somewhere. Otherwise, if people lose faith in elections, what remains of a democracy? Elections are the very foundations of a democracy. If people lose faith in elections, why would they even participate in them? I feel the Election Commission and the government of India need to reflect on this,” Abdullah said.He also said the report raised questions about the functioning of the poll panel and referred to his earlier concerns over the electoral process.The BJP rejected the Opposition's allegations and defended the reported differences between the Election Commissioners.Addressing a press conference at the BJP headquarters, party spokesperson Sambit Patra said differing views during official deliberations showed that the poll panel was functioning democratically.“The media reports saying that the election commissioners shared differing views in official deliberations is a reflection of pure democracy,” Patra said.“If there is no communication and exchange of views among the election commissioners who conduct polls, the opposition parties would allege 'dictatorship' and call them 'yes men' of the government,” he said.Patra said the Election Commission's response showed that neither the poll panel nor other constitutional bodies were functioning under a “dictatorial rule”.“This shows that the Election Commission (EC) and all other constitutional bodies are functioning in a democratic manner and upholding the democracy of the country,” he said.Responding to the media report, the Election Commission said written notes, observations, technical suggestions and internal checks and balances were standard practices within a multi-member constitutional body.“The ECI is a constitutional body that functions under the strict mandate of Article 324 of the Constitution, statutory rules and established institutional conventions. The Commission operates as a multi-member constitutional body. Written notes, observations, technical suggestions and internal checks-and-balances are standard, ongoing practices designed to ensure complete transparency, legal compliance and operational rigour,” it said.The commission said all official orders, decisions and administrative directions carried full legal sanction and followed established statutory procedures. It added that operational queries or inputs raised by members during the drafting stage were part of standard administrative practice aimed at safeguarding voter rights and improving electoral processes.The EC further said differing views and observations were a normal part of deliberation before a final decision was taken.“Not only the three Commissioners, but every officer of the Commission is fully authorised to give his suggestions to the Commission for improving the electoral system,” it said.The commission said focusing on specific internal notes and observations over 10 months while overlooking its wider body of approvals, decisions, instructions and initiatives presented only one part of the picture.It said it had taken numerous decisions, issued instructions and introduced around 40 new initiatives and electoral reforms, including electoral-roll revision and SIR across the country.“All these decisions are an outcome of the unanimous decisions of the full Commission in the past one year,” the EC said.The commission also pointed to the conduct of elections in Bihar, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Assam and West Bengal during the period and said it remained committed to carrying out its constitutional duties.
Article Summary: Opposition parties demand action against chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. They also demand an immediate halt to the SIR exercise and fresh elections in states where polls have already been held. The ruling BJP, however, defended the Election Commission, saying differences expressed by Election Commissioners during internal deliberations showed the poll panel was functioning democratically.

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court said Wednesday allegations of Bar Council of India's assets being transferred to a trust created by the BCI chairperson are a matter of concern and it has to be examined. SC also agreed to examine whether it has the power to establish and regulate law colleges and universities.The court was hearing petitions questioning the functioning of BCI-Pearl First Trust and the establishment of law colleges by the trust. Article Title: Judges appointing judges is a myth, says Justice Datta, points to way in which govt clears collegium picks
Article Text:
Judges appointing judges is a myth, says Justice Datta

NEW DELHI: Holding that the collegium system remains the most viable option for safeguarding judicial independence despite its "opacity and imperfections", Justice Dipankar Datta Wednesday said its deficiencies could not justify ushering in executive participation in collegium deliberations. He said judiciary had been relegated to playing second fiddle to the executive in appointments because of the way collegium recommendations were cleared by govt.Referring to govt's argument that the judiciary had an exclusive say in judges' appointments, Datta said "judiciary cannot always be at the receiving end" and devoted six pages to the issue, saying "relevant observations in response need to be made, lest the silence be misunderstood as a tacit acceptance by the court of such unworthy criticism in circulation".Datta said the executive wielded decisive control and held the reins over appointments at every level. He said it had become fashionable to blame the collegium for every infelicitous choice, conveniently forgetting that aberrations were exceptions and not the norm, and that no system could guarantee infallibility of human choice.The other judge on the bench, Justice S C Sharma said SG Tushar Mehta's submission was "not a criticism of the collegium system or regarding the role of executive in the appointment of judges"."It was a submission to the effect that if the constitution bench has held the presence of outsiders in collegium as violative of doctrine of separation of powers, a similar independence should be read in executive and rules framed under Art 324 be not declared void on the ground that it does not have an outsider in the selection committee or the executive predominates in it," he said.Sharma said the SG had based his argument on the judgment in the National Judicial Appointments Commission case, where a constitution bench held that the presence of even the law minister in the collegium for appointment of SC and HC judges would violate separation of powers. "Building upon the constitutional principle, the submission of the SG was that a corresponding degree of constitutional independence must be recognised for the executive as well as legislature. He submitted that the committee constituted under rules framed under Art 324 deserves to be declared legal though dominated by members of executive," Sharma said.Datta said, "The oft-repeated phrase that 'judges appoint judges' is a myth, which people have been fed by vested interests through motivated narratives. A sweeping generalisation that collegium acts as a law unto itself overlooks the consultative process envisaged under the Constitution, and the intrinsic role of executive - both at Centre and in the states."He added, "It is undeniable that collegium system has occasionally faltered and its functioning has not been free from aberrations. However, vociferous criticism, by itself, does not offer an alternative.While absence of an outsider may invite scrutiny, executive supremacy cannot be the cure. The constitutional quest is not to transfer primacy from one organ to another, but to preserve independence through checks and balances."What is worrying is that the sanctity of a collegium resolution is lost each time the executive implements it selectively, approving majority of those recommended while withholding one. Undeterred by piecemeal approvals and fate of those not cleared by the executive, collegium chooses to proceed, to avoid a head-on conflict with the executive, left with a Hobson's choice to keep the institution running. What it averts is a constitutional crisis; but the larger question is: how long can this state of affairs continue, if selective implementation is allowed to acquire the character of an accepted practice?"
Article Summary: Justice Dipankar Datta said the executive wielded decisive control and held the reins over appointments at every level. He said it had become fashionable to blame the collegium for every infelicitous choice, conveniently forgetting that aberrations were exceptions and not the norm. Datta devoted six pages to the issue, saying "relevant observations in response need to be made"
